source.title: Understanding Contextual Recall in Transformers: How Finetuning Enables In-Context Reasoning over Pretraining Knowledge
source.authors: Bhavya Vasudeva; Puneesh Deora; Alberto Bietti; Vatsal Sharan; Christos Thrampoulidis

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions induction heads as a prior account of ICL, but its experiments study synthetic contextual recall and task-vector representations; it does not test induction-head formation or the repeated-token copying behavior in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on contextual recall and task vectors, not induction heads. Those results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; they do not establish whether induction heads form or explain the behaviors specified in the claim. Mentions of induction heads in the related-work discussion are citations or background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The paper studies synthetic contextual recall, where a model must infer an attribute type from subject-attribute examples, plus the task-vector representations that come with it. It never identifies, measures or ablates induction heads or previous-token heads, and has no repeated-token copying measure. It mentions induction heads only as one of two prior proposed ICL mechanisms. Its 1-layer mechanism uses 'subject' and 'relation' heads, not induction heads.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Pretraining yields factual recall but not contextual recall. Targeted finetuning on tasks needing implicit inference, using a subset of subjects, makes contextual recall emerge on all subjects, with attribute-type task vectors. The authors also give a 1-layer subject/relation-head construction, validated empirically. They name task vectors, not induction heads, as the mechanism in their setting, but do not test induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses synthetic subject-grammar-attribute data, contextual-recall evaluations, and task-vector/mechanistic analyses; it does not apply the original induction-head detection or training-dynamics method.
record.method_sensitivity: Contextual-recall performance varies with pretraining sequence length, Markov-chain diversity, number of pretraining subjects, finetuning data format, and number of finetuning subjects. Representation clustering varies with demonstrations and Markov-chain diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining on PT sequences gives near-zero accuracy on ICL sequences. Finetuning on ICL or short variable-grammar ICL+Grm sequences with a subset of subjects generalizes to held-out subjects. Layer-2 attention representations cluster by attribute type, more strongly with more demonstrations and higher Markov-chain diversity, and can steer outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a synthetic contextual-recall task, finetuning induces task-vector representations that carry implicit attribute-type inference. The authors present this as a task-vector rather than induction-head mechanism, which is only loosely related to V6.

fits_no_version.finding: In 1-layer attention-only models, factual and contextual recall are implemented by a subject head (suppresses non-subject attributes) and a relation head. Finetuning repurposes the relation head to attend to in-context attribute tokens. Head-output cosine similarities match the constructions (Figs. 9–12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot attribute-type inference can be implemented by non-induction attention heads (subject/relation heads) in small attention-only models.

record.problems: The evidence is from a controlled synthetic task and small transformers. Several plotted results are described qualitatively rather than with exact values in the text; experiments in Sections 3.2–3.3 average across two initialization seeds, with no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: No induction-head results were reported. Other contextual-recall results about varying pretraining sequence length, Markov-chain diversity, subject counts, finetuning subject counts, and attribute coverage are not separately tabulated here; the paper describes their trends in Section 3.3 and Figs. 5–7, 13–14.

untested.parts: No induction heads, previous-token composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying are examined. The 1-layer attention-only constructions use subject and relation heads with no K-composition.
No induction-head formation over training, phase change, in-context loss gain or loss bump is measured.
No measurement of induction heads' share of ICL, or of loss by token index, in any model size.
No induction-head detection across families, sizes, seeds or modalities.
Data properties (Div, S, M, number of finetuning subjects) are varied, but only contextual-recall accuracy and task-vector clustering are measured, not induction-head formation.
The authors say task vectors, not induction heads, drive success on their task. But they never measure or ablate induction heads, so the relative contribution is untested.
Not examined. The stage-wise learning in pretraining concerns factual recall (attribute type, then exact attribute), not induction-head formation.

record.verdict_notes: The only induction-head content is background: two prior proposed ICL mechanisms, then 'task vectors is the mechanism' for this task. That is not a measurement of induction heads, so no verdict is given on V6 or any other version. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'].

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test induction heads, composition with a previous-token head, or [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying.
It does not measure induction-head formation over training, a phase change, token-index loss gains, or a corresponding loss bump.
It does not test whether induction heads explain most ICL in large transformers or measure loss falling with token index.
It does not test induction behavior across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
It varies data and finetuning for contextual recall but does not measure whether or when induction heads form or whether their formation depends on those choices.
It studies contextual recall, not few-shot task learning versus repeated-token copying, and does not test the relative contribution of induction heads.
It does not examine induction-head formation as one or multiple transitions.

rows.subject: 2-layer, single-head, decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated next-token accuracy on ICL sequences after PT training
rows.note: The text states this model learns factual associations on PT sequences but does not transfer that performance to ICL sequences. This is contextual recall, not the claim's repeated-token copying measure.

rows.subject: 2-layer, single-head, decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Finetuned on ICL sequences using a subset of subjects

conditions.value: ICL sequences with held-out query subjects

rows.baseline: Pretraining-only model has near-zero ICL accuracy
rows.value: The model learns contextual recall and generalizes to held-out subjects; numerical value shown in Fig. 3
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes successful generalization; the plotted numerical value is not stated in the text.

rows.subject: 2-layer, single-head, decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Finetuned on ICL+Grm sequences with short, variable grammar lengths

conditions.value: ICL sequences with held-out query subjects

rows.baseline: Pretraining-only model has near-zero ICL accuracy
rows.value: The model successfully generalizes to ICL sequences with held-out subjects; numerical value shown in Fig. 4
rows.note: The authors report successful generalization despite a prompt-format shift. The result is contextual recall, not induction-head copying.

rows.subject: 2-layer, single-head, decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured layer-2 attention-representation clustering by shared attribute type

conditions.value: increased; values include 0, 2, 10, and up to 15 in supplementary plots

rows.measure: Clustering strength of representations by attribute type
rows.value: Clustering strength increases with the number of demonstrations and with greater separation between attribute-specific Markov chains
rows.note: This measures task-vector-like representations for contextual recall, not induction heads.

rows.subject: 2-layer, single-head, decoder-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Interpolated a source context representation with a target attribute-type task vector to steer model output
rows.measure: Rank of original versus target attribute in predicted probabilities
rows.value: As beta increases, output is steered toward the target; the lower-Div setting requires a much larger beta
rows.note: This is a task-vector steering result for contextual recall; it does not measure induction behavior.
